summary: First-byte stalls on chat completions after model variant swap and batch policy change
description: Issue summary: Customer TactfulAI reports a sharp rise in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions in production immediately after our scheduled model variant swap and a batch policy change deployed to us-east. Impact: ~30% of sessions from the customer experience >2s first-byte delays, several user sessions saw streaming timeouts. Environment: prod/us-east, serving fleet for enterprise customers on Dedicated capacity. Observed behavior: elevated queue_wait_ms, increased request latencies, streaming connections that start but do not produce the first token for 1.5-3s. Expected behavior: first token emitted within typical 150-400ms baseline for equivalent prompts. This issue began after the change window on 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC where routing started preferring quantized model variants and adaptive batch policy was enabled for certain session classes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create chat session against customer's endpoint (prod/us-east) using pinned model variant redwood-alpha-v2-quant
2) Send a short prompt (~30 tokens) and request streaming responses with default timeout
3) Observe server accepts connection but first token latency often >1.5s; sometimes streaming connector times out after 3s
4) Re-run same prompt forcing model variant to non-quantized redwood-alpha-v2 and set batch_policy=fixed -> first token latency returns to baseline ~200ms
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: quantized model variant introduced slower small-batch startup for short sequences because of different kernel path and increased batching leading to queueing delays.

Observed queue_wait_ms spikes correlate with adaptive batcher selecting larger batch sizes for the session class used by the customer. Short prompt lengths are sensitive: larger batches increase first-token latency while improving throughput for long requests.
Profiling runtime hot path shows higher latency in kv-cache initialization for quantized kernel (q4_1) compared to fp16 variant for short sequence lengths.
Kernel telemetry: increased context switching and memcopy time on a subset of GPU instances after kernel change in runtime/pull/4521.
Routing logs show requests were re-routed from pinned non-quant nodes to newly labeled quantized pool due to updated variant scoring in rollout, concurrent with batcher policy flip.
Repro on staging: reproduced TTFB spike when combining quantized variant + adaptive batched policy. Pinning to fixed small batch size or non-quantized variant reduces TTFB to baseline.
Related previous tickets: SUP-31421 had similar pattern after runtime/model swap; suggests rollout gating was insufficient.
Risk assessment: ongoing sessions may see intermittent timeouts; broader exposure limited to customers routed to quantized pool in us-east. Not a universal fleet-wide outage.

Next steps planned: short-term mitigation: revert adaptive batcher for enterprise sessions and pin customer's routing to non-quant variant. Mid-term: runtime patch to fast-path small batch start for quantized kernels; improve rollout canary metrics to include per-customer TTFB and queue_wait_ms.
Assigned eng owners: Liam Chen (serving runtime), Priya Das (batcher/scheduler)

resolution_notes: Short-term: pinned tenant routing and reverted adaptive batch policy for enterprise session class. Medium-term: merged batcher tweak to respect small-sequence fast-path and runtime micro-optimization to reduce KV init overhead for q4_1 kernels. Follow-ups: update rollout checklist to require per-tenant TTFB and queue_wait_ms canaries, add automatic rollback threshold for TTFB regressions, inform Customer Success of timeline for full fix.
